dv.{{raw:headline}}: Neither improver beat two plain attempts on ARC-AGI-2

blocks.orig_inner: Can an AI coach teach itself to coach better?
blocks.md: Can an AI coach teach itself to coach better?

blocks.orig_inner: An AI coach rewrites the code of a puzzle-solving AI, the player, to make it better. We let the coach rewrite itself too, then tested whether the self-improved coach trains better players.
blocks.md: An AI **coach** rewrites the code of a puzzle-solving AI, the **player**, to make it better. We let the coach rewrite *itself* too, then tested whether the self-improved coach trains better players.

blocks.orig_inner: It does not. On an exam of 120 unseen puzzles, coached players scored about the same as an uncoached one. Letting the model simply think longer beat all coaching.
blocks.md: It does not. On an exam of {{int:sets.heldout_tasks}} unseen puzzles, coached players scored about the same as an uncoached one. Letting the model simply think longer beat all coaching.

blocks.orig_inner: The player is a short program that solves a puzzle with at most two model calls.11"Player" and "coach" are the repository's task agent and meta agent. Both use the same model. The coach looks at how the player did on 25 practice puzzles and edits the player's code. One such round is a generation. In step 1, the coach may also edit its own code, so it can get better at coaching.
blocks.md: The player is a short program that solves a puzzle with at most two model calls.[^1] The coach looks at how the player did on {{int:sets.source_practice_tasks}} practice puzzles and edits the player's code. One such round is a **generation**. In step 1, the coach may also edit its own code, so it can get better at coaching.

blocks.orig_inner: A coach edits the player's code. Then we let the coach edit its own.
blocks.md: A coach edits the player's code. Then we let the coach edit its own.

blocks.orig_inner: Step 1: the coach improves itself over many generations. Step 2: we freeze it and test it on a fresh player.
blocks.md: Step 1: the coach improves itself over many generations. Step 2: we freeze it and test it on a fresh player.

blocks.orig_inner: Figure 1: how the experiment works.
blocks.md: **Figure 1**: how the experiment works.

blocks.orig_inner: We ran step 1 6 times for 12 generations each. To test a coach, we froze it (either the original coach or the self-improved one from each run22From each run we took the self-edited coach whose players improved most on practice. The rule was fixed before any exam result existed [2].) and gave it a fresh, untouched player and 8 rounds on another 25 practice puzzles. The finished player then sat the exam once: 120 puzzles it had never seen.33The 120 public ARC-AGI-2 evaluation tasks [1], with 167 test inputs. A puzzle with several test inputs gives partial credit.
blocks.md: We ran step 1 {{int:n_source_seeds}} times for {{int:derived.sourceGens}} generations each. To test a coach, we froze it (either the original coach or the self-improved one from each run[^2]) and gave it a fresh, untouched player and {{int:derived.rounds}} rounds on another {{int:sets.payoff_practice_tasks}} practice puzzles. The finished player then sat the exam once: {{int:sets.heldout_tasks}} puzzles it had never seen.[^3]

blocks.orig_inner: For comparison, the uncoached player also sat the exam as it was, and once with the model set to think longer (reasoning effort one step higher), still with two calls and two answers per puzzle. No coach could change that setting.44A gateway no agent could edit fixed the model, its reasoning effort (high; xhigh for the think-longer run), the call cap and the budget.

blocks.orig_inner: The study did not record what the model was thinking. One difference: the demo asked for “detailed” reasoning summaries, the study for “auto” (which returned none in a short test). We show the only round, of several tried, that changed the player without breaking it, and two puzzles picked to illustrate: one the edit fixed and one it did not. Runs are not deterministic, so each player was run on each puzzle several times.

blocks.orig_inner: Noise. There were only 3 to 6 runs per group. One unchanged coach scored 26.0%, 27.8% and 36.0% in three tests, and several later picks were the same code as earlier ones.

blocks.orig_inner: The original coach needed adapting. With the repository's instruction as written, the model only asked clarifying questions. We added one sentence ("work autonomously") and loosened tool-call parsing. Both kinds of coach started from this adapted version.
